claim.anchor: Asbestos Hills, Northern Cape, South Africa — crocidolite-bearing banded iron formation; Heaney-Fisher antitaxial crack-seal interpretation
claim.description: Execute the Heaney & Fisher (2003) model: quartz and crocidolite grow synchronously in an antitaxial crack-seal seam, then a later oxidizing overprint changes the colour without consuming the crocidolite fibres.

deterministic.reason: Miyano and Klein's metamorphosed-iron-formation stability field permits crocidolite-to-amosite competition as temperature rises and alkalis escape.
An Fe-carbonate precursor/accessory is compatible with metamorphosed banded iron formation and is non-diagnostic beside the amphibole seam.
Quartz framework grows synchronously with crocidolite in the authored antitaxial crack-seal interpretation.
A subordinate Fe-oxyhydroxide is plausible only during the late oxidizing overprint.
BIF-host hematite and late oxidation products are geologically licensed, although discrete hematite nucleation is not required by this interpretation.
Hydrated silica is a possible late low-temperature competitor during oxidation, subordinate to the crack-seal quartz framework.

sources: Heaney P.J. & Fisher D.M. (2003) — New interpretation of the origin of tiger's-eye. Geology 31(4):323-326. DOI 10.1130/0091-7613(2003)031<0323:NIOTOO>2.0.CO;2. Synchronous antitaxial quartz-crocidolite crack-seal model; explicitly rejects pseudomorphic quartz replacement.

Miyano T. & Klein C. (1983) — Evaluation of the Stability Relations of Amphibole Asbestos in Metamorphosed Iron-Formations. Mining Geology 33:213-222. DOI 10.11456/shigenchishitsu1951.33.213. Crocidolite/amosite stability and BIF assemblages at 150-450°C.
notes: This scenario is one of a deliberately paired hypothesis test. Heaney & Fisher (2003, Geology 31:323-326) reject quartz pseudomorphism after pre-existing crocidolite and interpret synchronous quartz-crocidolite growth by antitaxial crack-seal vein filling.

The initial 300°C condition lies inside Miyano & Klein's (1983) 150-450°C low-to-medium-temperature amphibole-asbestos stability field. Pressure 1.0 kbar is a disclosed generic low-grade-metamorphic boundary, not locality barometry.

At step 58 exhumation carries the seam to the simulator's 0.001 kbar atmospheric floor and into a shallow oxidation window. Crocidolite remains solid in this model; tiger's-eye colour develops across the preserved crack-seal fabric. The 60°C value is a declared numerical weathering proxy, not measured Asbestos Hills fluid-inclusion thermometry.
Shape seed 2003 is authored independently from gameplay seed 42 and records the publication year of the modeled hypothesis.
